newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares drop on bomb attack,seen recovering.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares drop on bomb attack,seen recovering.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Wednesday, reversing morning gains after two bombs ripped through an outdoor market in Jewish west Jerusalem, killing 13 people.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 1.05 percent, or 3.22 points, to 302.33 on high all-share turnover of 240 million shekels against 226 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.17 percent lower at 309.87.
In the morning the Maof had risen by as much as 0.73 percent.
"Right after we heard about the attack and about the size of the attack people began selling," said Ilan Doron of Solid Financial Markets.
"I don't think, though, that this marks a change in trend. This was a spontaneous reaction to an event like this."

"The blast changed everything and the immediate reaction was to start selling. But it is only an emotional reaction and the market might resume its rise on Thursday," said a trader at Tachlit Securities.
Doron said that in the past the market has usually fallen in the first day or two after such an attack, but then completely recovers.
"In the long term such attacks don't affect the market," Doron said. He said he expected share prices to resume their upward path.

The Tachlit trader said that the market will wait to see how foreign investors will react. "This shouldn't change the trend but we have to wait and see what the foreign reaction is. The foreigners may want to wait a few days to see where the peace process is going," he said.
He noted that right after the attack foreign investors started buying aggressively. "Local investors were selling and the foreigners were buying."

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which rose 3.75 percent to 39,733 agorot (Israeli cents) on volume of 15.2 million shekels; Bezeq Israel Telecom, which surged 5.25 percent to 1,094 agorot on turnover of 7.2 million shekels; and Israel Corp, which gained 3.25 percent to 23,660 agorot on volume of 6.2 million shekels.
The Tachlit trader said that all the active shares rose on foreign buying. "Only the shares that are identified with foreign investors rose today," he said.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
